content:
We all know the folks that fully embrace Halloween and all the fanfare that goes hand in hand with the spooky holiday. A quick drive through nearly any neighborhood reveals an array of scary decorations and eerie inflatables to celebrate the season. I’ve never exactly been one to
enjoy haunted houses and the like, but watching kids run around in their costumes and collecting the most candy possible has always been a joy to experience.

I suppose it’s the season for scary stories.

A tale that has transcended time and logic has been the legend of Bigfoot. Also known as Sasquatch to many, the mysterious beast has a storied history throughout the land and has struck fear into countless hikers, farmers, campers and other unexpecting victims.

The history and lore behind Bigfoot is substantial. The large ape-like man of the woods was well-known in Native American culture and stories revolving around Sasquatch were passed down for generations. Some tribes believed him to be the keeper of the forest and a blessing on this Earth. Other tribes thought seeing a Bigfoot was a forewarning of danger and a precursor to a disastrous event. Some tribes, such as the Apache, believed the monsters to be akin to a devil and needed to be killed immediately.

Perhaps the most famous sighting was captured in the northern California woods in 1967 on 16mm film. What became known as the Patterson-Gimlin film has been the hallmark evidence of the large ape-like creature and has been reviewed countless times. In fact, a new documentary, “Capturing Bigfoot,” unveils a brand-new 4K scan of the footage. Along with the updated footage, the new film claims to debunk the classic evidence as a fraud.

While most are undoubtedly skeptical, there is something to be said about so many people from around the country seeing some type of creature. Are we surrounded by liars? Are people naturally drawn to see things that aren’t really there? Or are people genuinely seeing something lurking in the woods?

Frankly, sightings and encounters are a rather normal occurrence. According to the Bigfoot Field Researchers Organization (BFRO), there have been documented encounters in every state except Hawaii. Some states, such as Washington and Florida, have several hundred incidents where unsuspecting people discover the hairy creature. Here in Tennessee, we’ve had over 100 various encounters across the state.

The BFRO also has documented occurrences all around Middle Tennessee. Specifically, an incident in Maury County was a harmless encounter and had two people discover a Bigfoot just south of the Duck River and bordering on TVA land. The two unsuspecting hikers reported the creature being around 20 feet away and greeting them with a snarl and scream. They went on to claim they were aware the Bigfoot was often around the land and grew accustomed to his presence, but they considered it harmless since it never showed any aggression.

Another local account, from Lawrence County, showcases another interesting experience with the elusive critter. A native of the town of Ethridge recounts growing up with a Bigfoot that the family dubbed “Whistling Paddy.” Known to whistle and holler throughout the evening, the congenial animal developed a relationship with the family where they’d regularly provide food, particularly potatoes and other scraps, every evening around dusk.

This specific account details that Paddy was a regular around the farm. Standing nearly seven feet tall and having white hair with red-tinted eyes, Paddy would leave giant tracks all over the homeplace on a regular basis. The large family, including the neighbors, all knew of him and respected his routine and presence.

Of course, not all sightings and accounts are as peaceful as these two. Hikers, loggers and other people have claimed that they’ve been targets of these creatures’ aggression. Some report the throwing of large stones or branches. Others have claimed to be herded or corralled out of the location by a family of Sasquatches.

There are stories involving homeowners being terrorized by the cryptic beasts. With windows being smacked throughout the night, dogs being snatched, and objects being hurled.

There are even individuals that are completely sold that Bigfoot is responsible for grisly murders that have been blamed on other woodland animals, such a wolves. When a child disappears in the woods, people are quick to suspect Sasquatch as a prime suspect in the crime. The size, power and mystery surrounding the creature has produced a fear around the possibility of their existence.

In this season full of fun and fright, I enjoy exploring some of the historical lore that we still have. Perhaps these Sasquatch experiences are the product of overactive imaginations partnered with a penchant for lying, but the possibility exists that people are telling the truth.

In this case, the best we can do is to embrace the unknown.

Seth James Campbell is from Columbia and is an educator. He also runs Hound Dog Holler Animal Rescue. He has degrees from Columbia State Community College, University of Tennessee and Trevecca Nazarene University. He can be reached at sethjcampbell74@gmail.com.
